content.value: Section presets: assemblies, not atoms.

The utilization study found authors reach for structure and retreat to paragraphs. These four presets are the counter-move: named, copy-paste block assemblies for the four sections every serious paper needs. Copy the JSON, replace the <angled> placeholders, publish.
Preset: masthead — kicker to TOC in seven blocks
The opening rhythm of /papers/portabledoc-potential-study and the criminality essay: eyebrow, display h1, ingress standfirst, byline topics, a 4-tile stat wall (use
denom
for the compact a/b read), divider, linked toc. Anchors point at blocks-block-<index> container ids.
Preset: figure — a chart that argues

A chart block with the annotation layer: region washes narrate zones, a refLine carries the target, a point callout names the peak. Tones: info, ok, warn, danger. The caption states the claim the figure earns and its source - never just a title.
Preset: dashboard — queries, not numbers
Three stat queries in columns, a bars chart over closed_at weeks, a task board. Swap <epic-id> and publish; the reader resolves every block live and re-renders on task events. Full contract:
the cookbook
; working proof:
the flagship
Preset: runbook — steps that can fail honestly
Numbered steps with terminal transcripts, a verification step whose check can actually fail, and the rollback callout written before you need it.
Distilled from the papers shipped during the PortableDoc delivery wave (2026-07-22). Studio insert-palette versions of these presets are the filed follow-up; until then this page is the palette.

The adoption counter-move to the utilization study's finding that authors reach for structure and retreat to paragraphs: hand them assemblies, not atoms.
